# =============================================================================
# tessera-term: SGR attributes incl. 256-colour, truecolour, underline styles and underline colour (issue #7, wave 4)
# crates/tessera-term/tests/fixtures/sgr_spec.txt   (spec-researcher output)
#
# Evidence file for the implementer and the critic.  Companions (same directory layout, copied next to it):
#   tests/fixtures/sgr_color_table_cells.txt   expected per-cell styles of the colour table (433 groups)
#   tests/scripts/sgr/color_table.txt          the colour-table script (27x80), fed like the other scripts
#   tools/ (NOT copied)                         model.py = an independent Python model of the semantics below that
#                                               every Part A row was cross-checked against; gen_color_table.py
#
# FORMAT
#   Part A (pen rows): one row per line, `ID | feed | pen [| free]`, preceded by `# cite:` / `# note:` lines.
#     feed   `tests/common` `decode` syntax (\x1b \r \n \\ \u{..}), fed to a fresh 24x80 Terminal.  `++` separates
#            separate Terminal::advance calls; the pen (Grid::pen()) is read after the last one.
#            EVERY row must give the same result when the feed is sent one byte per advance() call.
#     pen    canonical pen text (below).
#     free   the row documents a divergence or an undefined case: parse it, do NOT assert it.
#   Part C (cell rows): `### ID` blocks: size / feed (one per step) / cell: (row,col) 'char' pen / cursor /
#     pending_wrap / extra keys.  Unlisted cells are NOT asserted unless the block says `others: blank`.
#     Special chars: '<spacer>' = the right half of a wide char, `wide` / `cluster` after a char = CellFlags.
#   Canonical pen text (a renderer local to tests/sgr.rs prints exactly this; independent of Style's bit layout):
#     fg=<c> bg=<c> ul=<c> us=<style> flags=<list>
#     <c>      `-` Color::Default | `iN` Color::Indexed(N) | `#rrggbb` Color::Rgb (lower case)
#     <style>  none | single | double | curly | dotted | dashed       (Style::underline_style())
#     <list>   `-` or comma list in this order: bold,dim,italic,blink,inverse,hidden,strike,overline,superscript,
#              subscript (the last three added by #81)
#              (the UNDERLINE and four *_UNDERLINE bits are shown only as us=, never in flags=)
#     default pen: fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=-
#
# PRIMARY SOURCES (read in full for this fixture)
#   xterm ctlseqs   https://invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html  "CSI Pm m"
#   xterm source    https://github.com/ThomasDickey/xterm-snapshots  (master, charproc.c $XTermId 1.2134)
#                   charproc.c CASE_SGR (l.4322-4590), parse_extended_colors (l.2122) with its long design comment,
#                   param_has_subparams (l.2020), CASE_REP (l.6157), `sp->lastchar = thischar` (l.6485),
#                   CASE_DECALN (l.4837), resetRendition (l.1388); cursor.c CursorSave2 / CursorRestoreFlags;
#                   screen.c ClearCells (erase keeps the colour pair, not the rendition flags)
#   ECMA-48 5th     https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-48/
#                   8.3.117 SGR; 5.4.2 parameter string format (":" inside a parameter sub-string)
#   ITU-T T.416 / ISO 8613-6   SGR 38/48 with 5 = indexed, 2 = direct colour, colour-space id after the 2 (section
#                   number 13.1.8 is from memory; the standard is paywalled and was read only through xterm's
#                   design comment above parse_extended_colors, l.2035-2120)
#   kitty           https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/underlines/  (4:0..4:5, 58 "works exactly like 38, 48", 59;
#                   terminfo `Su`) and source kitty/vt-parser.c _parse_sgr, kitty/cursor.c parse_color +
#                   cursor_from_sgr
#   WezTerm         wezterm-escape-parser/src/csi.rs  CSIParser::sgr, parse_sgr_color, underline
#   Alacritty/vte   https://github.com/alacritty/vte  src/ansi.rs  attrs_from_sgr_parameters, handle_colon_rgb,
#                   parse_sgr_color
#   (iTerm2 was not read; its documented behaviour for 4:x and 58/59 is kitty's.  Not relied on for any row.)
#
# EMULATOR MATRIX  (tess = recommended Tessera behaviour; D-* are the decisions below)
#   topic                          xterm                kitty               WezTerm              Alacritty          tess
#   4:x sub-parameter              IGNORED (group       4:0..4:5, clamp     0..5, else single    0,2,3,4,5; any     kitty/Alacritty
#                                  skipped, even 4:3)   >5 to dashed                             other 4:n single   (D-US-UNK)
#   21                             double underline     double              double               CANCEL BOLD        double
#   22                             clears bold+faint    both                both                 both               both
#   24                             clears 4 and 21      clears decoration   clears all           clears all         every style
#   5 / 6                          both blink           5 only (6 ignored)  slow / rapid         slow / fast        both = BLINK (D-BLINK6)
#   8 / 28                         yes                  not handled         yes                  yes                yes
#   58 / 59                        NOT SUPPORTED        yes                 yes                  yes                yes (lead decision 1)
#   38;5;n, n > 255                whole colour no-op   n & 0xFF (wraps)    Err (to_u8)          no-op              no-op (lead decision 4)
#   38;2;r;g;b, any > 255          no-op                each & 0xFF         Err                  no-op              no-op
#   38;7;.. unknown kind           eats `38;7`, goes on drops WHOLE SGR     Err                  eats `38;7`, goes  eats kind (D-38-UNK)
#                                                                                                on
#   1:2 colon group, other head    group ignored        applies head (bold) not traced           group ignored      ignore (D-SUB-OTHER)
#   too few values for 38/48       consumes to the end  group dropped       Err                  consumes to end    consumes to end
#   `38;5;` empty index            DEFAULT => no-op     index 0             -                    index 0 (vte)      index 0 (F-EMPTY-IDX)
#   38;5:1 mixed separators        accepted             accepted            -                    not accepted       whatever falls out
#   SGR between print and REP      cancels REP          -                   -                    keeps last char    cancels REP (D-REP)
#   BCE (erase colour)             colour pair, no      bg only             bg only              bg only            bg only
#                                  rendition flags
#   DECRC without DECSC            default rendition    -                   -                    -                  default pen
#
# DECISIONS FOR THE MILESTONE LEAD  (recommended option first; rows that depend on them are named)
#   D-US-UNK    `4:n` with n > 5.  Recommend: plain single underline (Alacritty, WezTerm).  kitty clamps to dashed,
#               xterm ignores the group.  Rows US4c6/US4c9/US4c65535.
#   D-SUB-OTHER A colon group headed by anything but 4, 38, 48, 58 (`1:2`, `3:1`, `0:1`, `:1`, `31:1`).
#               Recommend: ignore the whole group (xterm: `item += skip`; Alacritty: `_ => None`); kitty applies the
#               head.  Matters because `params` is flattened: a naive loop would see `1`,`2` = bold + faint and
#               `0:1` = reset + bold.  Needs the `subparams` bitmask in sgr(): after a head, skip every following
#               param whose bit is set.  Rows SUB_*.
#   D-38-UNK    `38;<kind>` with kind not 2 or 5.  Recommend: eat `38;kind` and continue with the next param
#               (xterm, Alacritty).  kitty ignores the whole SGR.  Rows 38_unknown_kind, 38_kind_zero,
#               38_kind_1_eats_kind_only, 48_unknown_kind, UL58_unknown_kind.  Lead decision 4 does not say.
#   D-BLINK6    SGR 6 (rapid blink).  Recommend: same BLINK flag as 5 (xterm); 25 clears it.  Row ATT06.
#   D-REP       Any SGR clears State::last_printed, so `A ESC[31m ESC[3b` prints one A (xterm l.6485; already how
#               main behaves, csi_spec.txt D-REP).  The brief's "SGR under REP" therefore cannot show REP picking up
#               a new pen.  Rows REP01..03.  No change needed; keep the rule when adding sgr.rs (do not make
#               State::apply special-case 'm').
#   D-EMPTY     Empty parameter slots arrive from vte as 0, so `38;5;` is Indexed(0) and `38:2:1::3` is rgb(1,0,3),
#               where xterm treats the slot as DEFAULT and drops the colour.  Recommend: accept (parser limit),
#               rows are `free`.
#   D-MIXED     `38;5:196` / `38;2:1:2:3` (colon inside a semicolon list).  xterm and kitty accept, Alacritty does
#               not.  Recommend: do not special-case; a ';'-form reader that consumes flattened params regardless
#               of the tail's bits accepts them for free.  Rows are `free`.
#   D-LEN       More than 32 parameters: tessera-vt already sets ignore:true and Terminal drops the whole action
#               (xterm keeps 30, kitty 100).  Recommend: keep.  Rows LEN_*.
#   D-SAVED     DECSC/DECRC save and restore the whole Style, underline colour included, and DECRC without a prior
#               DECSC gives the default pen (xterm zeroed slot).  No code change (Grid::save_cursor copies `pen`).
#
# ISSUE / BRIEF CORRECTIONS (verified against sources)
#   1. "xterm as the reference" covers only the 0..9, 21..29, 30..49, 90..107 and 38/48 rows.  xterm has NO 58/59 at
#      all (it would read `58;5;1` as blink + bold) and IGNORES every colon group except 38/48, so `4:0`..`4:5`
#      are not an xterm behaviour: the reference for 4:x, 58, 59 is kitty (docs + source), cross-checked with
#      WezTerm and Alacritty.  Expected values for those rows are kitty's.
#   2. "SGR under REP" (see D-REP): REP is a no-op after SGR in xterm and on main; the REP rows document that.
#   3. Brief decision 4, "too few parameters for 38/48/58 (xterm consumes what exists and stops)": true for 38/48;
#      for 58 xterm has no code, so the rule is borrowed from 38/48 (kitty drops the group; same visible result).
#      Values > 255: xterm, Alacritty and WezTerm make the colour a no-op, kitty wraps (`& 0xFF`).  The brief's
#      choice (no-op) is the majority, so the kitty-derived rows for 58 deliberately differ from kitty.
#   4. Colour-space disambiguation is by sub-parameter COUNT, not by emptiness: after the head, 4 sub-parameters
#      (`2:r:g:b`) = no id, >= 5 = id in the slot after the 2 (empty or not, value ignored), anything beyond the
#      third colour value is dropped.  `38:2:1:2:3:4` is rgb(2,3,4), not rgb(1,2,3).  The ';' form has NO id:
#      `38;2;0;1;2;3` is rgb(0,1,2) then italic (SGR 3).  (xterm l.2035-2120, kitty parse_color, Alacritty
#      handle_colon_rgb all agree.)
#   5. vte (tessera-vt) turns empty slots into 0 and a trailing `;` into an extra 0 parameter: `ESC[1;m` is bold
#      then RESET (xterm identical: DEFAULT == 0), `ESC[1;;3m` is italic only, `ESC[;1m` is bold.  A trailing
#      empty slot resetting the pen surprises people; the rows RST06..RST08 pin it.
#   6. SGR 21: Alacritty implements it as "cancel bold" (the pre-1990 reading).  Brief and xterm say double
#      underline; so do kitty and WezTerm.  Alacritty is the odd one out.
#   7. `CSI > 4 ; 2 m` (XTMODKEYS), `CSI ? 4 m`, `CSI 1 SP m` are not SGR.  State::csi already returns early when
#      `intermediates` is non-empty (csi.rs l.70-79), which covers them; keep that check ahead of the new 'm' arm.
#      Rows NOT_SGR_* pass for free as long as that order is kept.
#   8. Follow-ups outside #7 (all since done): the terminfo entry advertises `Su`/`Smulx`/`Setulc` (ADR 0005, kitty
#      docs name `Su`); DECSTR (`CSI ! p`) resets SGR as in xterm (#80).
#      SGR 53/55 (overline) and 73-75 (superscript/subscript) were ignored here; #81 adds the flags (rows OL_, VA_,
#      OV_, RS_, TR_, CS_, UK_, HX_ and blocks OLC01-06 below).
#
# PARSER FACTS (probed against vte 0.15, the version tessera-vt wraps)
#   `ESC[m` -> groups [[0]]            `ESC[1;m` -> [[1],[0]]         `ESC[;1m` -> [[0],[1]]    `ESC[1;;3m` -> [[1],[0],[3]]
#   `ESC[4:3m` -> [[4,3]]              `ESC[4:m` -> [[4,0]]           `ESC[4::3m` -> [[4,0,3]]  `ESC[:1m` -> [[0,1]]
#   `ESC[38:2::1:2:3m` -> [[38,2,0,1,2,3]]   `ESC[38:2:1:2:3m` -> [[38,2,1,2,3]]   `ESC[38:2:::1:2:3m` -> [[38,2,0,0,1,2,3]]
#   `ESC[38;5:1m` -> [[38],[5,1]]      `ESC[1;4:3;5m` -> [[1],[4,3],[5]]
#   `subparams` bitmask (bit i <=> params[i] came after ':'):  `4:3` -> params [4,3] bits 0b10;
#   `38:2::1:2:3` -> [38,2,0,1,2,3] bits 0b111110; `1;4:3;5` -> [1,4,3,5] bits 0b100; `ESC[m` -> [0] bits 0.
#   `ESC[>4;2m` -> intermediates [62]; `ESC[?4m` -> [63]; `ESC[1 m` -> [32].
#   65536 and 99999999999 saturate to 65535.  33 parameters (colon-separated entries count too) set ignore:true.
#
# =============================================================================

# #############################################################################
# PART A / B : PEN ROWS
# #############################################################################

# ---- A1. Reset (SGR 0, empty list, empty slots) ----------------------------------------------------------
# cite: ECMA-48 8.3.117 (default 0); xterm ctlseqs; xterm CASE_SGR `case DEFAULT: case 0`
# note: bare CSI m; vte gives params [0]
RST01_empty_csi_m | \x1b[m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=-
# cite: xterm CASE_SGR resetRendition + reset_SGR_Colors; kitty cursor_reset_display_attrs
# note: after bold dim italic underline blink inverse hidden strike fg bg and underline colour
RST02_empty_resets_everything | \x1b[1;2;3;4;5;7;8;9;31;42;58;5;9m++\x1b[m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=-
# cite: ECMA-48 8.3.117; xterm CASE_SGR
# note: lead decision 5: 0 also resets the underline colour and every underline style
RST03_zero | \x1b[1;2;3;4;5;7;8;9;31;42;58;5;9m++\x1b[0m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=-
# cite: xterm CASE_SGR DEFAULT==0 for each empty slot
# note: [0],[0]
RST04_semicolon_only | \x1b[1;2;3;4;5;7;8;9;31;42;58;5;9m++\x1b[;m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=-
# cite: xterm CASE_SGR params are applied left to right
# note: bold and red are wiped by the 0, italic survives
RST05_reset_in_the_middle | \x1b[1;31;0;3m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=italic
# cite: xterm CASE_SGR trailing empty parameter is DEFAULT => reset
# note: vte yields [3],[0]; `ESC[3;m` is italic THEN reset
RST06_trailing_semicolon_resets | \x1b[1m++\x1b[3;m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=-
# cite: xterm CASE_SGR empty middle parameter is DEFAULT => reset; vte (and so Alacritty) turns an empty slot into 0
# note: bold, reset, italic.
RST07_empty_in_the_middle_resets | \x1b[1;;3m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=italic
# cite: xterm CASE_SGR
# note: [0],[3]
RST08_leading_empty_resets | \x1b[1m++\x1b[;3m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=italic
# cite: lead decision 5
# note: curly underline and RGB underline colour both cleared
RST09_reset_keeps_nothing_underline_style | \x1b[4:3;58:2::1:2:3m++\x1b[0m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=-

# ==== #81 addendum: overline (53/55), superscript/subscript (73/74/75) ====================================
# Source: spec-researcher addendum 2026-10-28 (mintty termout.c do_sgr, WezTerm wezterm-escape-parser csi.rs and
# wezterm-cell; xterm, kitty and Alacritty implement none of the five codes and ignore them).  Lead decisions
# (brief #81): 73/74 are mutually exclusive as in WezTerm (mintty keeps two independent bits); only 0 or an empty
# parameter clears the three flags; a colon group headed by 53/55/73-75 is ignored whole (D-SUB-OTHER).
# ---- OL. overline on / off ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# cite: ECMA-48 8.3.117 (53 overlined); mintty termout.c l.2313; WezTerm SgrCode::OverlineOn
OL_01_on | \x1b[53m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=overline
# cite: ECMA-48 8.3.117 (55 not overlined); mintty l.2314; WezTerm OverlineOff
OL_02_on_off_one_sgr | \x1b[53;55m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=-
OL_03_on_off_two_sgrs | \x1b[53m++\x1b[55m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=-
# note: 55 on a default pen is a no-op
OL_04_off_when_off | \x1b[55m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=-
OL_05_on_twice | \x1b[53;53m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=overline
OL_06_off_then_on | \x1b[55;53m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=overline
OL_07_on_off_on | \x1b[53;55;53m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=overline
OL_08_on_survives_next_sgr | \x1b[53m++\x1b[1m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=bold,overline

# ---- VA. superscript / subscript ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# cite: mintty termout.c l.2268; WezTerm SgrCode::VerticalAlignSuperScript (73)
VA_01_super | \x1b[73m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=superscript
# cite: mintty l.2269; WezTerm VerticalAlignSubScript (74)
VA_02_sub | \x1b[74m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=subscript
# cite: mintty l.2270 (75 clears both); WezTerm VerticalAlignBaseLine (75)
VA_03_super_then_75 | \x1b[73;75m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=-
VA_04_sub_then_75 | \x1b[74;75m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=-
# note: 75 on a default pen is a no-op
VA_05_75_when_off | \x1b[75m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=-
# cite: D-VA-EXCL -- WezTerm single enum (wezterm-cell vertical_align); mintty would give BOTH bits (divergence, recommendation)
VA_06_super_then_sub_exclusive | \x1b[73;74m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=subscript
VA_07_sub_then_super_exclusive | \x1b[74;73m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=superscript
VA_08_super_sub_75 | \x1b[73;74;75m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=-
VA_09_super_75_sub | \x1b[73;75;74m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=subscript
VA_10_super_twice | \x1b[73;73m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=superscript
VA_11_exclusive_across_sgrs | \x1b[73m++\x1b[74m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=subscript
VA_12_flip_flop | \x1b[74;73;75;73m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=superscript

# ---- OV. independence: overline vs super/sub, and the other attributes -------------------------------------
# cite: mintty (separate ATTR_ bits); WezTerm (overline bit 12 vs vertical_align bits 15-16)
OV_01_over_and_super | \x1b[53;73m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=overline,superscript
OV_02_over_and_sub | \x1b[53;74m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=overline,subscript
# note: 75 clears super/sub ONLY (mintty l.2270 mask); 55 clears overline ONLY
OV_03_75_keeps_overline | \x1b[53;73;75m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=overline
OV_04_55_keeps_super | \x1b[53;73;55m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=superscript
OV_05_74_keeps_overline | \x1b[73;53;74m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=overline,subscript
# cite: mintty l.2293-2301 (21 = double underline, 24 = clear underline mask); xterm 24 clears UNDERLINE|DBL_UNDER; no emulator touches overline
OV_06_21_keeps_overline | \x1b[53;21m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=double flags=overline
OV_07_24_keeps_overline | \x1b[53;4;24m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=overline
OV_08_21_then_24_keeps_overline | \x1b[53;21;24m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=overline
# note: added by the implementer (#81): 21 and 24 leave superscript/subscript alone too (mintty do_sgr 21/24 touch UNDER_MASK only;
# note: WezTerm Sgr::Underline only)
OV_08b_21_keeps_super | \x1b[73;21m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=double flags=superscript
OV_08c_21_24_keep_overline_and_sub | \x1b[53;74;21m++\x1b[24m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=overline,subscript
OV_09_55_keeps_underline | \x1b[4;53;55m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=single flags=-
OV_10_24_keeps_super_sub | \x1b[73;4;24m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=superscript
OV_11_curly_underline_with_super | \x1b[73;4:3m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=curly flags=superscript
OV_12_curly_with_overline | \x1b[4:3;53m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=curly flags=overline
# note: underline colour 58/59 is independent of the three flags
OV_13_ul_colour_set_clear_keeps_overline | \x1b[53;58;5;9;59m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=overline
OV_14_ul_colour_with_overline | \x1b[53;4;58;5;9m | fg=- bg=- ul=i9 us=single flags=overline
OV_15_colours_with_flags | \x1b[31;42;53;74m | fg=i1 bg=i2 ul=- us=none flags=overline,subscript
OV_16_inverse_with_overline | \x1b[7;53m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=inverse,overline
# note: full house; underline off so the pen shows every non-underline flag
OV_17_every_flag | \x1b[1;2;3;5;7;8;9;53;73m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=bold,dim,italic,blink,inverse,hidden,strike,overline,superscript
OV_18_every_flag_sub | \x1b[1;2;3;5;7;8;9;53;74m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=bold,dim,italic,blink,inverse,hidden,strike,overline,subscript
OV_19_order_does_not_matter | \x1b[74;53;9;1m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=bold,strike,overline,subscript

# ---- RS. which resets clear the flags -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# cite: ECMA-48 8.3.117 (0 = default rendition); mintty l.2221 `attr = CATTR_DEFAULT`; WezTerm Sgr::Reset
RS_01_zero_clears_overline | \x1b[53m++\x1b[0m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=-
RS_02_empty_clears_super | \x1b[73m++\x1b[m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=-
RS_03_zero_clears_sub_and_overline | \x1b[53;74m++\x1b[0m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=-
RS_04_zero_in_the_middle | \x1b[53;73;0m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=-
RS_05_zero_then_set | \x1b[53;0;73m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=superscript
# cite: xterm CASE_SGR empty slot == 0 (sgr_spec.txt RST06..RST08, vte gives an extra 0)
RS_06_trailing_semicolon_resets | \x1b[53;m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=-
RS_06b_empty_slot_between | \x1b[53;;74m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=subscript
RS_06c_leading_empty_slot_then_set | \x1b[;53m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=overline
RS_06d_reset_clears_all_incl_new | \x1b[1;2;3;4;5;7;8;9;31;42;53;73;58;5;9m++\x1b[0m | fg=- bg=- ul=- us=none flags=-
# cite: D-RESET-SCOPE -- mintty do_sgr 22,23,24,25,27,28,29,39,49,59 do not mention OVERL/SUPERSCR/SUBSCR; WezTerm same

# PART D : COLOUR TABLE
# #############################################################################
# tests/scripts/sgr/color_table.txt (27x80) + tests/fixtures/sgr_color_table_cells.txt give the 16 ANSI colours as
# fg (30-37, 90-97) and bg (40-47, 100-107), the 6x6x6 cube (48;5;16..231, bg), the 24 greys (48:5 bg, 38;5 fg),
# truecolour ramps in all four spellings (`;`, `:` with empty id, `:` without id, `:` with id 7), truecolour fg,
# underline colours (58;5;n and 58:2::r:g:b with 4:1..4:5), and an attribute sampler.  Every group is 3 columns of
# label + SGR 0 + one default space.  Cite: xterm ctlseqs (256-colour layout: 0-15 ANSI, 16-231 cube
# 16+36r+6g+b, 232-255 greys); the expected styles are generated from the colour numbers, not from the script text.
# The snapshot the implementer takes of this table is a regression pin; the cells file is the independent oracle.
